text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Norwegian spent 17 billion crowns last year on gambling, including lotteries and slot machines.

- Reformed Communist Gerd-Liv Valla has suddenly become justice minister after Anne Holt stepped down because of ill health. Holt's resignation weakens the minority Labour government of Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland.
- Family Minister Sylvia Brustad wants software developers to create more games for girls to make them interested in personal computers. Today it is mainly boys who like computers.
- Kvaerner ASA will soon sign a 6.5 billion crown contract with U.S. oil company Exxon to build an oil and gas platform for Russia's offshore Sakhalin project.

- State-owned oil company Statoil is distributing personal computers to 13,000 employees so that they can become computer literate. The deal is worth 210 million crowns for state-owned Telenor telecommunications company and computer firm Compaq.

- Shares in telecommunications group Nera ASA fell yesterday morning following the release of below-forecast annual results. The company said higher R&D expenditure and non-recurring costs for restructuring and expansion led to a six percent decline in 1996 operating profits.
